{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
    "line": 838,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by datetime but is wired to order_by=\"-datetime\"",
    "body": "OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value))` on the raw attribute value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (a millisecond integer). The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses it with order_by=\"-datetime\", so `value` is a datetime and math.floor() raises TypeError on the first page; even if that were fixed, build_queryset would compare the datetime column against a bare integer cursor value, producing wrong results or DB errors. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to handle this conversion. Any superuser/admin requesting the audit log with optimized_pagination=true will get a 500. The paginator should subclass/reuse DateTimePaginator's key conversion or the endpoint should not use it for datetime ordering."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
    "line": 880,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Negative-offset branch slices queryset with a negative start, which Django does not support",
    "body": "In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0 (which any caller can produce by supplying a cursor string like \"<value>:-5:0\", since Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers), the code executes `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start index. Django's QuerySet explicitly rejects negative slicing and raises AssertionError (\"Negative indexing is not supported\"), turning a client-supplied cursor into an unhandled 500. The comment claiming \"the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically\" is false. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError like the other paginators do."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
    "line": 63,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "ZPOPMIN silently discards spans (possibly including the root span) once a segment exceeds 1000",
    "body": "The new eviction `redis.call(\"zpopmin\", set_key, span_count - 1000)` drops the spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise from the segment with no metric, log, or error. Previously, oversized segments were skipped at flush time with an error log and the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric (code removed from _load_segment_data in buffer.py). Now spans are silently deleted from the segment, so downstream consumers receive truncated traces with no signal. Worse, because scores are end timestamps, the root span often finishes last... but a long-running root that ended early relative to children can be evicted while the span-buf:hrs flag stays set, so the segment is flushed on the fast root-timeout path with its root span missing and is_segment recomputed at flush time as false for every span. At minimum this needs a metric/log and a decision about protecting the root span."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
    "line": 62,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Eviction threshold hardcoded to 1000, desynced from configurable max_segment_spans (default 1001)",
    "body": "The Lua script caps segment size at a hardcoded 1000, while SpansBuffer keeps the configurable `max_segment_spans` parameter (default 1001) which is now dead code after the removal of the span-count check in _load_segment_data. Operators who tuned max_segment_spans will silently get a different limit, and the two values disagree (Lua evicts down to 1000, the Python default says 1001), so a segment can be capped at 1000 spans even though configuration says 1001 are allowed. Either pass the limit into the script as an ARGV or remove the unused parameter."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
    "line": 30,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Redirect-follow loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without migration or justification",
    "body": "The redirect resolution loop was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`. Existing segments in Redis can already have redirect chains deeper than 1000 (created while the 10k limit was in effect); for those traces, lookups now stop after 1000 hops, so new spans are written to a new span-buf:s: set keyed at the truncated chain end instead of merging with the real segment. That splits one trace into two separately flushed segments (duplicated/partial segments downstream). The removed comment explicitly acknowledged this tradeoff at 10k; the change needs either a migration/drain plan or a comment and metric for the hit-limit case."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
    "line": 71,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "organization_context.member may be None for non-superuser requests, causing AttributeError",
    "body": "The gate `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` whenever the user is not a superuser. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional (e.g., org auth tokens or certain access paths where no organization member object is attached to the context). In that case this raises AttributeError and returns a 500 instead of simply not enabling the optimized path. Use `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access`."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
    "line": 449,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "No test covers the new zset eviction-at-1000 behavior or its interplay with flush",
    "body": "The PR changes segment storage from sets to sorted sets and adds eviction of spans beyond 1000 in add-buffer.lua, but the added test lines only thread end_timestamp_precise through existing tests. There is no test that (a) inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment and asserts which spans survive eviction, (b) verifies behavior when the evicted span is the root/is_segment span, or (c) checks that eviction interacts correctly with the queue timeout. Given the silent data loss this introduces, the eviction semantics should be pinned down by tests."
  }
]}

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by datetime but is wired to order_by="-datetime"
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value))` on the raw attribute value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (a millisecond integer). The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses it with order_by="-datetime", so `value` is a datetime and math.floor() raises TypeError on the first page; even if that were fixed, build_queryset would compare the datetime column against a bare integer cursor value, producing wrong results or DB errors. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to handle this conversion. Any superuser/admin requesting the audit log with optimized_pagination=true will get a 500. The paginator should subclass/reuse DateTimePaginator's key conversion or the endpoint should not use it for datetime ordering.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch slices queryset with a negative start, which Django does not support
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0 (which any caller can produce by supplying a cursor string like "<value>:-5:0", since Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers), the code executes `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start index. Django's QuerySet explicitly rejects negative slicing and raises AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported"), turning a client-supplied cursor into an unhandled 500. The comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError like the other paginators do.

findings.title: ZPOPMIN silently discards spans (possibly including the root span) once a segment exceeds 1000
findings.body: The new eviction `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` drops the spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise from the segment with no metric, log, or error. Previously, oversized segments were skipped at flush time with an error log and the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric (code removed from _load_segment_data in buffer.py). Now spans are silently deleted from the segment, so downstream consumers receive truncated traces with no signal. Worse, because scores are end timestamps, the root span often finishes last... but a long-running root that ended early relative to children can be evicted while the span-buf:hrs flag stays set, so the segment is flushed on the fast root-timeout path with its root span missing and is_segment recomputed at flush time as false for every span. At minimum this needs a metric/log and a decision about protecting the root span.

findings.title: Eviction threshold hardcoded to 1000, desynced from configurable max_segment_spans (default 1001)
findings.body: The Lua script caps segment size at a hardcoded 1000, while SpansBuffer keeps the configurable `max_segment_spans` parameter (default 1001) which is now dead code after the removal of the span-count check in _load_segment_data. Operators who tuned max_segment_spans will silently get a different limit, and the two values disagree (Lua evicts down to 1000, the Python default says 1001), so a segment can be capped at 1000 spans even though configuration says 1001 are allowed. Either pass the limit into the script as an ARGV or remove the unused parameter.

findings.title: Redirect-follow loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without migration or justification
findings.body: The redirect resolution loop was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`. Existing segments in Redis can already have redirect chains deeper than 1000 (created while the 10k limit was in effect); for those traces, lookups now stop after 1000 hops, so new spans are written to a new span-buf:s: set keyed at the truncated chain end instead of merging with the real segment. That splits one trace into two separately flushed segments (duplicated/partial segments downstream). The removed comment explicitly acknowledged this tradeoff at 10k; the change needs either a migration/drain plan or a comment and metric for the hit-limit case.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None for non-superuser requests, causing AttributeError
findings.body: The gate `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` whenever the user is not a superuser. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional (e.g., org auth tokens or certain access paths where no organization member object is attached to the context). In that case this raises AttributeError and returns a 500 instead of simply not enabling the optimized path. Use `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access`.

findings.title: No test covers the new zset eviction-at-1000 behavior or its interplay with flush
findings.body: The PR changes segment storage from sets to sorted sets and adds eviction of spans beyond 1000 in add-buffer.lua, but the added test lines only thread end_timestamp_precise through existing tests. There is no test that (a) inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment and asserts which spans survive eviction, (b) verifies behavior when the evicted span is the root/is_segment span, or (c) checks that eviction interacts correctly with the queue timeout. Given the silent data loss this introduces, the eviction semantics should be pinned down by tests.
